questions.question: Compare features of Arduino and Raspberry Pi.
questions.answer_html:
Comparison: Arduino (Uno) vs. Raspberry Pi (Single-Board Computer)

Although both boards are iconic open-hardware platforms used in prototyping and IoT, they are fundamentally different computational species:

  • Arduino (Uno) is a Microcontroller Development Board designed to interface directly with sensors, actuators, and hardware pins to execute repetitive low-level real-time firmware loops.
  • Raspberry Pi (e.g., Pi 4/5) is a complete Single-Board Computer (SBC) powered by a high-speed multi-core microprocessor that runs a full desktop operating system (Linux).

Parametric Comparison Table

Comparison Parameter Arduino Uno (Rev 3) Raspberry Pi (e.g., Model 4B)
Device Classification Microcontroller Development Board Single-Board Computer (SBC)
Primary Processor Core 8-bit AVR RISC CPU (Microchip ATmega328P) Quad-core 64-bit ARM Cortex-A72 (Broadcom BCM2711)
Clock Frequency 16 MHz 1.5 GHz to 1.8 GHz (over 100x faster!)
System RAM (Volatile) 2 KB (0.000002 GB) internal SRAM 1 GB, 2 GB, 4 GB, or 8 GB LPDDR4 SDRAM
Program / Storage Space 32 KB internal Flash memory External MicroSD card, USB 3.0 SSD, or NVMe PCIe (16 GB to 1 TB+)
Operating System Execution No Operating System (Bare-Metal). Code executes directly on the bare metal hardware in an infinite loop(). Full Multi-Tasking OS: Raspberry Pi OS (Debian Linux), Ubuntu, Windows 10 IoT Core.
Real-Time Determinism Hard Real-Time Deterministic. Clock-cycle accurate execution of timing pulses, interrupts, and PWM without OS jitter. Non-Deterministic (Soft Real-Time). Linux kernel thread preemption introduces variable scheduling jitter (milliseconds).
Analog-to-Digital Conversion (ADC) Built-in 10-bit ADC with 6 dedicated analog input pins (A0–A5). Reads sensors directly! No Native ADC. GPIO pins are purely digital (3.3V logic). Reading analog sensors requires an external ADC IC (e.g., MCP3008 via SPI).
Power Consumption & Supply Ultra-low power (~150 mW, 45 mA at 5V). Can be easily powered from a 9V battery or solar cell. High power (3.5 W to 15 W, requires 5V @ 3A USB-C power supply); active cooling fan recommended.
Boot Time Instantaneous (< 0.5 seconds); starts executing sketch immediately upon power-up. Slow (15 to 45 seconds to boot the Linux kernel and user space).
Display & Multimedia Ports None (only basic serial monitor over USB; small character LCDs via SPI/I2C). Dual 4K micro-HDMI ports, Gigabit Ethernet, 2x USB 3.0, 2x USB 2.0, CSI camera port, DSI display port.
Programming Languages C / C++ (via the Arduino IDE / AVR-GCC toolchain). Python, C, C++, Java, Node.js, Go, Rust, Bash shell scripting.
Typical Best-Fit Applications Motor position control, reading analog temperature/light sensors, simple robots, LED controllers, relay switches. Computer vision (OpenCV face recognition), Edge AI / machine learning, media servers, home automation hubs, web servers.

Synergistic Integration (Working Together)

Because Arduino and Raspberry Pi possess complementary strengths, advanced embedded engineering projects frequently combine both:

Autonomous Mobile Robot Architecture:
• Raspberry Pi (The "Brain"): Runs Linux, processes camera video feeds using OpenCV, plans navigation paths, and hosts a web dashboard.
• Arduino (The "Limbs"): Connected to the Pi via USB/Serial; handles sub-millisecond PID motor speed control, reads ultrasonic ping sensors, and emergency stop bumper switches.

questions.question: Extended libraries of Arduino.
questions.answer_html:
Extended Libraries of Arduino

An Arduino Library is a modular, reusable collection of C++ classes, functions, and definitions designed to abstract complex microcontroller hardware registers, bus timing protocols, and communication sequences behind an intuitive, human-readable Application Programming Interface (API).

1. Concept & Architecture of Arduino Libraries

Without libraries, an embedded developer would need to manually manipulate dozens of low-level hardware registers, configure clock prescalers, and calculate bit masks (e.g., setting TWCR, TWDR, TWSR registers for I2C). An Arduino library packages this low-level register manipulation into a reusable object-oriented class. An Arduino library consists of:

  • LibraryName.h: C++ Header file containing class declarations, function prototypes, pin definitions, and constants.
  • LibraryName.cpp: C++ Source implementation file containing the operational algorithms, register writes, and ISR bindings.
  • keywords.txt: Syntax highlighting configuration file for the Arduino IDE text editor.
  • examples/: Directory containing ready-to-run .ino example sketches demonstrating usage.

2. Key Standard & Extended Arduino Libraries

Library Name Header Include Target Hardware / Protocol Key Methods & Architectural Purpose
1. Wire Library #include <Wire.h> I2C / TWI (Two-Wire Interface) Communication Enables communication with I2C sensor chips (accelerometers, RTCs, OLED displays) over SDA/SCL pins:
• Wire.begin(): Initializes I2C bus as master or slave.
• Wire.beginTransmission(address): Begins queuing data for target slave.
• Wire.write(val): Queues bytes for transmission.
• Wire.endTransmission(): Transmits queued bytes and sends I2C STOP condition.
• Wire.requestFrom(address, count): Reads data bytes back from slave.
2. SPI Library #include <SPI.h> SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) Bus High-speed synchronous serial data communication with external Flash, SD cards, and RF transceivers (NRF24L01):
• SPI.begin(): Configures SCK, MOSI, and SS pins.
• SPI.transfer(byte): Simultaneously transmits and receives a byte in one cycle.
• SPI.beginTransaction(SPISettings(speed, bitOrder, mode)): Configures bus clock speed and polarity.
3. Servo Library #include <Servo.h> RC Hobby Servomotors (0° to 180°) Controls standard hobby servo motors by using ATmega328P hardware Timer1 to generate high-precision 50 Hz PWM signals (1.0 ms to 2.0 ms pulse widths) without CPU intervention:
• servo.attach(pin): Associates pin with timer channel.
• servo.write(angle): Commands servo to turn to specific angle (0–180°).
• servo.read(): Retrieves current servo shaft position.
4. LiquidCrystal Library #include <LiquidCrystal.h> Alphanumeric LCD Displays (Hitachi HD44780) Drives popular 16x2 and 20x4 character LCD modules using 4-bit or 8-bit parallel digital interfaces:
• LiquidCrystal lcd(rs, en, d4, d5, d6, d7): Instantiates LCD with pin map.
• lcd.begin(cols, rows): Initializes display dimensions.
• lcd.setCursor(col, row): Moves text cursor.
• lcd.print("Hello"): Outputs text to screen.
• lcd.clear(): Wipes display RAM.
5. EEPROM Library #include <EEPROM.h> Internal 1 KB Non-Volatile EEPROM Reads and writes persistent bytes to on-chip EEPROM surviving power outages:
• EEPROM.read(address): Reads 1 byte from address (0–1023).
• EEPROM.write(address, val): Writes 1 byte (consumes write cycle).
• EEPROM.update(address, val): Smart write: Reads first, only writes if value changed, saving EEPROM write endurance!
• EEPROM.put(addr, struct) / EEPROM.get(addr, struct): Saves and retrieves entire custom C structs.
6. SoftwareSerial Library #include <SoftwareSerial.h> Software Emulated UART Allows bit-banging asynchronous serial UART communication on virtually any pair of general-purpose digital pins using pin-change interrupts, freeing the single hardware USART for USB debugging:
• SoftwareSerial mySerial(rxPin, txPin)
• mySerial.begin(9600); mySerial.println().
7. SD Library #include <SD.h> FAT16 / FAT32 MicroSD Cards Mounts SD cards via SPI bus and exposes a file-system interface for data logging:
• SD.begin(cspin): Mounts filesystem.
• File file = SD.open("log.csv", FILE_WRITE): Opens file.
• file.println(); file.close().
8. WiFi / Ethernet Library #include <WiFi.h> / <Ethernet.h> TCP/IP Network Stack Provides client/server sockets, HTTP client requests, DNS lookup, and DHCP IP lease handling for connected IoT shields.

3. Illustrative Code Example: Integrating Multiple Libraries

#include <Wire.h>           // For I2C communication
#include <LiquidCrystal.h>  // For LCD display
#include <EEPROM.h>         // For persistent parameter storage
#include <Servo.h>          // For mechanical actuation

LiquidCrystal lcd(12, 11, 5, 4, 3, 2);
Servo gateServo;

void setup() {
  Wire.begin();             // Join I2C bus as master
  lcd.begin(16, 2);         // Initialize 16x2 LCD
  gateServo.attach(9);      // Attach servo control to Pin 9
  
  byte lastPos = EEPROM.read(0); // Restore saved position from EEPROM
  gateServo.write(lastPos);
  
  lcd.setCursor(0, 0);
  lcd.print("System Online");
  lcd.setCursor(0, 1);
  lcd.print("Servo Pos: ");
  lcd.print(lastPos);
}

void loop() {
  // Application tasks execute with abstracted simplicity
}
